families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer/polyol hosts retain a phosphoric-acid-rich polar phase to preserve hydrogen-bonded proton pathways into the cold window.
descriptor_match: D2: DES/plasticiser and hydrated acid motifs support bound polar-fluid continuity at low temperature.
D3: starch/PVA/chitosan-type hosts are flexible, hydrogen-bonded film formers rather than brittle inorganic matrices.
D4: phosphoric acid or acid-containing DES can remain in non-crystallising complexed states under confinement.
D6: abundant OH/NH sites and acid species provide dense donor/acceptor relay landscapes.
D7: biopolymer hosts are reported to retain water/acid without immediate structural failure.

families.family_description: Fibrous or tubular inorganic hosts confine and retain phosphoric-acid-rich phases while guiding interconnected proton-transport channels.
descriptor_match: D4: phosphoric-acid-containing confined phases and DES-like acid complexes are plausible cold-stable proton sources.
D5: attapulgite and halloysite directly evidence 1-D nanoconfinement and channel guidance.
D6: retained phosphoric acid provides hydrogen-bond-mediated proton transfer.
D7: clay/tubular hosts are reported to reduce leaching and immobilise the conducting phase.

families.family_description: Amorphous protonated phosphate domains combined with organic hydrogen-bonding phases aim to avoid crystallisation and maintain continuous proton mobility.
descriptor_match: D1: phosphate glass is explicitly described as an amorphous continuous proton-transport medium.
D4: protonated phosphate networks offer non-crystalline acid-like proton environments.
D6: phosphate groups and OH-rich additives create dense relay landscapes.
D7: glassy phosphate networks strongly retain proton-bearing species, though hydration dependence remains a risk.

instances.composition_description: A starch/PVA blend lightly doped with phosphoric acid as a flexible OH-rich proton-conducting film.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-water and plasticised continuity in an OH-rich blend
proton_relay: dense hydroxyl network plus PA should support hybrid hopping/vehicular transfer
retention: low PA loading is more likely to limit leaching than heavily doped films
risk_flags: PA leaching if acid loading is increased

element_evidence.reason: Starch is directly reported as an OH-rich hydrogen-bond channel former and compatibility-promoting blend component.
PVA contributes an OH-mediated donor/acceptor network in starch blends.
PA is the proton source, with low-doping retention-focused use reported as more stable than high loading.

instances.novelty_rationale: Retained as a control because starch-based phosphoric-acid films are already represented in the evidence pool. It anchors a low-complexity benchmark for the colder-targeted novel variants.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan membrane plasticised with a choline chloride/phosphoric acid deep eutectic to supply a non-crystallising proton-carrying phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: DES-like acid phase is plausible for bound polar-fluid continuity near 200 K
matrix_flexibility: chitosan plus DES should reduce brittle behaviour versus dry chitosan
acid_state: ChCl-complexed PA may remain more mobile than neat frozen acid/water domains
risk_flags: high water uptake may soften the film excessively
conductivity depends on maintaining DES homogeneity

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is reported to retain hydrated conducting phases without disintegration and to interact with acid-bearing transport scaffolds.
ChCl is directly evidenced as a complexing DES counter-species for phosphoric acid.
PA is evidenced both as a DES acid component and as a hydrogen-bond-mediated proton-conducting medium.

instances.novelty_rationale: The individual chitosan, ChCl/PA DES, and acid-conduction motifs are supported, but their direct combination is not explicitly present in the pool. It is novel mainly by pairing a biopolymer retention scaffold with a cold-favored complexed acid phase.

instances.composition_description: A quaternary membrane combining chitosan, PVA, 1-D attapulgite, and retained phosphoric acid to couple film flexibility with guided nanoconfined acid transport.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: 1-D attapulgite should guide interconnected acid-rich pathways
cold_window: PVA/chitosan host may preserve a plasticised hydrogen-bond network into the subambient range
retention: clay-hosted acid is plausibly less leachable than free acid in a neat polymer film
risk_flags: phase segregation between polymer blend and clay if mixing is poor
acid over-binding at clay sites could lower mobility

element_evidence.reason: CS is directly reported as a percolated acid-interacting scaffold aiding confinement and retention.
PVA provides an OH-rich hydrogen-bonding film-former analogous to other flexible proton-conducting blends.
Attapulgite is directly evidenced for 1-D nanoconfinement, channel guidance, and acid immobilisation.
PA is supported as both a mobile acid proton source in complexed form and as a hydrogen-bond-mediated conductor.

instances.novelty_rationale: This is the requested quaternary synergy motif: biopolymer host plus PVA-like film former plus 1-D clay plus phosphoric acid. The novelty lies in merging separately supported retention, flexibility, and nanoconfinement functions into one cold-oriented composite.

instances.composition_description: A starch matrix incorporating halloysite nanotubes preloaded or co-loaded with phosphoric acid to create retained tubular proton pathways.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: HNT lumens and interfaces plausibly retain acid-rich conducting domains
hydrogen_bonding: starch adds an OH-dense relay matrix around the tubes
retention: HNT-hosted PA should resist leaching better than freely dispersed acid
risk_flags: starch moisture sensitivity may change transport strongly with humidity
tube loading heterogeneity may interrupt percolation

element_evidence.reason: Starch is evidenced as an OH-rich channel-forming matrix with proton-transport-promoting oxygen groups.
HNTs are directly reported as PA hosts that provide nanoconfinement and reduced leaching.
PA is evidenced as a complexable acid proton source and as an active hydrogen-bond-mediated conductor.

instances.novelty_rationale: The pool supports starch-based proton-conducting matrices and PA@HNT confinement separately, but not this merged formulation. It is novel because the starch OH network is used as the external relay phase around a tubular retained-acid core.

instances.composition_description: A hybrid of protonated phosphate glass particles dispersed within a starch-rich matrix to combine amorphous proton-retaining domains with a flexible OH-rich binder.
components: phosphate glass (APS proton-substituted / protonated phosphate network)
expected_properties: pathway_continuity: amorphous phosphate domains may avoid discrete freezing transitions
proton_relay: glass phosphate groups plus starch OH sites should create mixed relay interfaces
retention: proton-bearing phosphate network is inherently immobilised relative to free acid
risk_flags: interfacial brittleness or poor particle dispersion
conductivity may depend strongly on residual hydration

element_evidence.component: phosphate glass (APS proton-substituted / protonated phosphate network)
element_evidence.reason: Protonated phosphate glass is directly evidenced as amorphous, proton-conducting, hydrogen-bond-active, and retaining the proton-bearing phase.
Starch contributes a dense OH network and channel-forming behavior analogous to flexible interfacial proton-relay binders.

instances.novelty_rationale: No direct glass-starch hybrid appears in the pool, but both components have supported proton-transport roles. The concept is novel because it softens an amorphous inorganic proton conductor with a cold-tolerant biopolymer interface rather than relying on free acid alone.
